title: Reflection (`reflect`): power, cost and when not to use it

videos.script: Everything you know about Go types is decided before the program runs. The compiler checks it, and then forgets it. Reflection is the way back. A program asks, while it runs, what type a value has, and reads or changes it through the answer. {{typeof}} First, what reflect sees. A value goes in as an any, two words: one for the type and one for the data. TypeOf and ValueOf read those two words, and nothing else. {{tags}} Then struct tags, which only reflection can read. You will read them the way encoding/json does, and build a column picker for hits on top of them. {{set}} Next, changing things. Reflection can set a variable and call a method by its name, but only through an address. Get it wrong and the program compiles, passes go vet, and panics. {{cost}} Last, the bill. A benchmark puts reflection beside plain code and generics, and a typo shows which version the compiler protects. This is the first of four escape hatches. Each one works. The lesson is about when to leave it shut.
